text:
incident-bot: ALERT: sudden memory creep detected on paged-attention allocator in prod-cluster-3. Multiple model-host pods reporting OOM kills and CUDA allocation failures. severity=P2. Affected service: runtime-serving (route: /v1/generate). See dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/1784309210 :warning:

maya: I see ~30% of gpu-host pods have restarted 1-3x in last 15m. Logs show repeated 'cudaErrorMemoryAllocation' + kernel messages about 'out of device memory'. Paging metrics show paged_attn_frag_ratio rising steadily from 0.12 -> 0.68 over 4h. KV-cache size also trending up.

samir: copying logs here: ```
[2026-06-02T22:05:12Z] runtime ERROR cuda: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation at allocator.c:492
[2026-06-02T22:05:13Z] runtime WARN OOM-killer triggered: pid=2378, rss=24.3GB, limit=24GB
[2026-06-02T22:06:01Z] runtime INFO paging: compact_candidates=0, free_frag=3.2GB, total_cache=18.4GB
```

kevin: customer impact: some 5xxs for long-context models (>8k) reported, latency spikes ~3-10s increased error rate on high-concurrency routes. CS flagged 6 customers, will loop in account reps. audrey-cs, please confirm list.

audrey-cs: Confirmed — accounts: acme-inc, medlytics, quickdocs. Impact window so far ~22:00-22:25 UTC. Customers hit primarily when requests include long prefix caching + streaming. Sending preliminary notification now. :email:

lisa: quick triage: looks like fragmentation + slow leak. Possibly paged-attn allocator not releasing KV pages when model context switches. I can push a hotfix to disable prefix caching for the most affected model variant (gptx-long-8k) as a mitigation. That should reduce KV cache churn.

maya: Mitigation plan (immediate):
- 22:12: disable prefix/KV caching for gptx-long-8k on prod (route-level config). Command: ```curl -XPOST "https://controlplane/api/v1/configs/disable_kv?model=gptx-long-8k" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN"```
- 22:15: reduce batch_size to 1 for that route (temporary)
- 22:17: scale up dedicated pool by +2 GPU nodes to buy time
- 22:20: cordon and drain node gpu-3-07 with highest RSS, restart runtime pod, check for leak reappearance

ops-runner: Executed scale-up (+2 nodes) and cordoned gpu-3-07. Draining now. current node restarts show containers restarting and clearing RSS. Observed one container core dumped at /var/crash/runtime-core. Uploading core to /artifacts/1784309210/core-gpu-3-07.dmp

infra-bot: Note: node gpu-3-07 has been cordoned and drained by ops-runner. Autoscaler override applied (temp +2).

samir: I've applied the prefix caching disable and lowered batch_size on the route. Watching memory graphs. Also set runtime env var RUNTIME_PAGEDATTN_COMPACTION=1 to trigger more aggressive compaction.

maya: After these mitigations, paging fragmentation dropped from 0.68 -> 0.32 over ~14m and OOMs reduced. A few pods still show elevated RSS (~20GB) but not growing. Latency normalizing. Still seeing occasional cuda allocation fails on one pod that had a core dump.

kevin: Sending customer update: "We've mitigated the immediate memory pressure by disabling prefix caching for long-context workloads and adding capacity. We're investigating a potential allocator fragmentation bug. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA for fix." Sending now.

audrey-cs: Sent to affected customers, asked for any logs/examples. Two customers reported that reducing input prefix length helped, one customer saw no further errors.

lisa: Debug notes for postmortem: suspect that paged-attention allocator fragmentation slowly leaks on context-switch heavy workloads due to stale KV entries not reclaimed when layer reuse happens. Repro on staging with synthetic traffic at high context churn. Will open a repro ticket with script and heap traces.

maya: Open action items (handoff to night oncall samir):
- Monitor cluster for next 8h, alert if paged_attn_frag_ratio > 0.45 for >10m
- Collect full set of core dumps + gdb backtraces for the three affected pods (paths in /artifacts/1784309210/)
- Run periodic force compaction script (one-time every 30m) until hotfix deployed: ```/usr/local/bin/compaction-trigger --cluster prod-cluster-3 --force```
- Coordinate with infra to set memory limit guardrail on runtime pods to 26GB to avoid noisy OOM churn
- Prep rollback plan to re-enable prefix caching after stable patch (depends on allocator fix)

samir: Taking shift. I'll watch dashboards and run compaction script every 30m. Posting checks to #pager-duties. If we see repeat OOMs, I'll drain additional nodes and bring online spare capacity. :eyes:

ops-runner: Note: I've uploaded pod logs + nvidia-smi captures to artifacts. Commands run: ```kubectl exec -it runtime-abc -- bash -c "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv"``` and ```pmap -x $(pidof runtime) | tail -n 20```

infra-bot: Reminder: file /artifacts/1784309210/ contains artifacts: core dumps, pmap outputs, nvidia-smi snapshots, docker-stats csv. Retention set to 30d.

kevin: Customer comms: follow-up postmortem will include timeline, mitigation, and expected fix ETA. Coordinating with product for formal RCA.

audrey-cs: I'll keep customer updates queued; will escalate to account leads if it reoccurs.

maya: Leaving notes in the incident board: severity downgraded to P3 at 22:35 UTC after stabilization. Will open bug: "paged-attn allocator: fragmentation + KV leak under context churn" and assign to eng-runtime. Add test harness for high-churn KV scenarios.

samir: Acknowledged handoff. Will update thread with any regressions. :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks team — if anything spikes, ping @samir and @ops-runner immediately. Good job stabilizing. :rocket:
